name: Warehouse fleet
summary: A picking warehouse of 3,400 m² with up to 60 mobile robots, real robot speeds, pick times and batteries, spills and robot faults, any layout, simulated live on the CPU, an NVIDIA GPU or Tenstorrent c
help: Runs a picking warehouse live for Minutes. The hall (65 x 53 m with the defaults, about 3,400 m²) has 20 pairs of rack rows in 5 blocks, one-way aisles, cross-aisles, highways at both ends, 8 pack-out stations on the south wall and docks with chargers along the walls; Layout changes it within the same hall (blocks=3, stations=6, stations_at=both, slotting=random), as the Warehouse layouts block compares them. Orders arrive (Order rate) with 1 to 3 lines; an idle robot with enough charge takes one, drives to each pick face, waits while the picker puts the item in its tote (Seconds to pick an item), takes the tote to the least busy station and waits while it is unloaded, then goes back to its dock. Batteries run down on the move and less standing; a robot below Go to charge below finishes its order and charges at its dock; idle robots charge too. The defaults follow real robots: MiR100 drives at up to 1.5 m/s, about 10 h on a charge, 2-3 h to charge; Locus Origin about 8 h, about 50 min to charge; collaborative picking 8-12 s per item. Incidents (Incidents per hour): a spill or a dropped item closes an aisle cell, or a robot stops with a fault where it is; someone comes after Minutes until someone comes (on average) and cleans up or repairs it; meanwhile the routes are planned around it. The times of the incidents are assumptions to set for your site, not measured figures. Routes come from distance fields of every target, computed on the machine's accelerator (CPU: SciPy breadth-first search; NVIDIA: wavefront on the GPU; Tenstorrent: TT-NN tile matmuls on the cards), and again whenever an aisle is closed or opened. Tenstorrent runs the robots' steps on the cards too when PyTorch/XLA for Tenstorrent (tt-xla) is installed, else on the CPU beside them; the Linux machine with the cards needs TT-NN in the worker's Python (pip install ttnn, the version of the cards' firmware). auto uses Tenstorrent cards when the machine has them, else an NVIDIA GPU, else the CPU; naming one makes the block stop if it is not there. Connect its telemetry to a 3D view: it draws the warehouse (layout, with the incidents), the robots with their battery and the items in their tote (fleet), the KPIs (kpi), where robots wait (heat) and what happened (event); and to a Run timeline for the events and the performance over time. Commands on the control channel, as the 3D view's Controls or a Controls view send them ({"control": NAME, "value": …}): order_rate, robots, speed, paused, block_aisle ([x, y]: blocks that aisle cell, or opens it again) and Open all aisles. Results: kpis.json, timeline.csv and events.json, warehouse.json.

inputs.label: Warehouse models
inputs.help: From Warehouse models: the run starts once the view has its models

outputs.label: KPIs
outputs.help: The run's totals: orders, lines, orders per hour, order time, robots busy, incidents, metres per item

outputs.label: Timeline
outputs.help: timeline.csv (every 30 simulated seconds) and events.json (what changed, incidents and their clearing)

params.label: Orders per hour at the start
params.help: Each order has 1 to 3 lines (items); about 40 robots serve 400 orders per hour in this hall

params.label: Simulation speed
params.help: Times real time; the view can change it

params.label: Minutes it runs
params.help: Real minutes; the run's Stop ends it before

params.label: Accelerator
params.help: auto: Tenstorrent cards, else an NVIDIA GPU, else the CPU of the machine that runs it

params.label: Layout
params.help: Changes to the layout in the same hall, as key=value: blocks=3 (rack blocks from front to back), stations=6, stations_at=both (south and north walls), slotting=random (popular products anywhere). Empty: the hall below as it is

params.label: Rack pairs
params.help: Double rows of racks across the hall, with one-way aisles between them (3 m each)

params.label: Rack blocks
params.help: Blocks of racks from front to back, with cross-aisles between them

params.label: Seconds to pick an item
params.help: Collaborative picking takes about 8-12 s per item

params.label: Seconds to unload at the station
Robot speed (m/s)
params.help: Warehouse AMRs drive at 1 to 1.5 m/s at most; 1.2 allows for slowing at turns

params.label: Hours on a charge
params.help: Working, on the move; standing uses about a third

params.label: Incidents per hour
params.help: Spills or dropped items that close an aisle, and robot faults; 0 for none

params.label: Minutes to clean up a spill
